clue.text: Picture of vessels turning round

indicators.note: turning here means the vessels are spun about so their name reads backwards

parts.note: pans are cooking vessels
a round of ammunition is a shot

explanation.surface: A photograph shows boats swinging about in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' is the reversal sign for the vessels. 'round' looks like a second half of that signal ('turning round'), but it is a single round fired from a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick photograph is a kind of picture.

clue.text: Poor Morton's love in Conrad's work

indicators.note: poor suggests the name is in a bad way, so its letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's still gives the letter S here, as the setter uses MORTONS whole
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A reader pities a character named Morton in one of Joseph Conrad's novels.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of MORTONS with O makes the title of Joseph Conrad's 1904 novel set in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad wrote the novel of that name, so it is one of his works.

clue.text: Churchmen appear before turn by stars

parts.note: pre- is the Latin-derived prefix meaning before
a bend is a turn in a road or river
Aries, the Ram, is a constellation of stars

explanation.surface: Clergy show up early before a heavenly conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: Prebendaries are canons holding a stipend from a cathedral, so they are senior clergymen.

clue.text: Perhaps use the middle of the verse ?

definitions.text: Perhaps use the middle of the verse ?

parts.words: Perhaps use the middle of the verse ?
parts.note: the central letters of the word verse are E and R, and saying er is what a speaker does while pausing for thought

explanation.surface: Advice to a poet about which lines of a poem to quote.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'middle of the verse' is not a poem's central stanza but the letters ER inside the word, the noise of someone pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying er is the sound of pausing in uncertainty, so using it means to falter before speaking.

clue.text: Flash follower?

parts.note: a flash of lightning is followed by the rumble of a storm

explanation.definitionFit: The crash of a storm comes after the lightning flash, so it follows the flash.

clue.text: Firm's requirement a sound forecaster

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for a forecaster is only to be heard, not spelt as written

parts.note: a prophet forecasts the future

explanation.surface: A business needs a reliable economic forecaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like the adjective 'reliable' describing the forecaster, but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm must make money over its costs to survive, so earnings above outlay are what it requires.

clue.text: A river, it appears in New Hampshire

indicators.note: appears in tells us the word it is set inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: NH is the postal abbreviation for the US state of New Hampshire
taken as written

explanation.surface: A river is said to turn up in New Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The river is not American at all: the Nith flows through Dumfriesshire in south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nith is a Scottish waterway flowing into the Solway Firth.

clue.text: Their fragrance is not intoxicating

parts.note: the flowers are named after tea, a drink that does not make anyone drunk, and their scent is likened to it

explanation.definitionFit: These roses are said to smell of tea, and tea is a non-alcoholic drink.

clue.text: The main dance band instruments?

definitions.meaning: the main is the sea, and this lively dance is associated with sailors
a horn and a pipe are both instruments a band might play

explanation.surface: Asking which instruments play the principal dance at a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the sea, as in the Spanish Main, not 'principal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailors' jig takes its name from an old wind instrument made of a horn and a pipe.

clue.text: Man for instance is back in Helsinki

indicators.note: back tells us the letters found are read in reverse order
in tells us the letters sit inside the word Helsinki

explanation.surface: A man is said to have returned to the Finnish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island.

clue.text: Great War artist — Scottish family man?

definitions.meaning: Bruce ... drew the Old Bill cartoons of soldiers in the trenches during the First World War
bairns is Scots for children, so their dad is a Scottish family man

explanation.surface: A First World War illustrator is described as a Scot with children.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairnsfather was a cartoonist of the 1914-18 war, and split up his name means the dad of Scottish children.

clue.text: Completely reversing reaction to spirits, perhaps

definitions.meaning: turning the tables is reversing a situation completely
at a seance a table is said to tilt and move in response to ghosts

explanation.surface: Someone does a complete about-turn after a drink of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' looks like strong drink; it is ghosts at a seance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both a complete reversal of fortunes and the movement of a seance table attributed to ghosts.

clue.text: Foot sore East lost way — see through that?

parts.note: a corn is a painful patch on the foot

indicators.note: lost tells us letters for a road are dropped from the compass point

parts.note: taken as the compass point, spelt out
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone with aching feet goes east, misses the road and needs to see where they are going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes ST (street) from EAST, leaving EA.
explanation.definitionFit: The transparent front layer of the eye is what light passes through, so vision is through it.

clue.text: What we get from a table in Centre Mess

definitions.text: What we get from a table in Centre Mess

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other
centre asks for the middle letters of the following word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner describes what they are served from the table in a central mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre Mess' looks like the name of a dining hall; 'Centre' asks for the middle letters of Mess, and 'in' puts the table piece inside them, so the clue as a whole also defines food.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is what is served at a table, and things fit to eat are foodstuffs.

clue.text: Formation of R.A.F. goes to get horses' supplies

indicators.note: a formation is an arrangement, so these letters are flown into a new order

parts.note: the Royal Air Force, abbreviated RAF

explanation.surface: An air force formation flies off to fetch fodder for horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formation' looks like aircraft flying together but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Forage is fodder for animals, so in the plural it means feed for horses.

clue.text: Discharged a politician ? Just gas!

parts.note: a gun that is fired is discharged
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A sacked politician is dismissed as nothing but hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just gas' looks like a jibe at a windbag; it defines a gas literally.
explanation.definitionFit: This explosive methane found in coal mines is simply a gas.

clue.text: French physicist's flowers brighten up bulbs

definitions.text: French physicist's flowers brighten up bulbs

parts.words: French physicist's flowers brighten up bulbs
parts.note: the flowers are things that flow, units of electric current named after the physicist Ampere, and current lights lamps

explanation.definitionFit: The units of electrical current carry the name of Andre-Marie Ampere, and current makes lamps glow.

clue.text: Note-maker is fellow scholar, about fifty-one

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: about tells us the scholar goes around the number

parts.note: a don is a university scholar
in Roman numerals L is fifty and I is one

explanation.surface: Someone who takes notes is a college fellow aged about fifty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note-maker' suggests a person taking notes, but it is a musical instrument making notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute-like stringed instrument produces musical notes.

clue.text: Strongly urged, the red ox went mad

indicators.note: went mad tells us the letters charge about into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal is goaded until a red ox runs amok.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone earnestly to act is to urge them strongly.

clue.text: Space traveller sent on set programme

definitions.text: Space traveller sent on set programme

parts.words: Space traveller sent on set programme
parts.note: the first communications satellite in orbit relayed television programmes on to sets across the Atlantic

explanation.definitionFit: The satellite launched in 1962 travelled through space and passed television signals between continents.

clue.text: Lee and Blair appear unusually trustworthy

indicators.note: unusually tells us the names appear in an unusual order of letters

explanation.surface: Two well-known men turn out to be oddly dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dependable can be trusted.

clue.text: Go in for crime?

parts.note: to go in, entering a house, with criminal intent is housebreaking

explanation.definitionFit: Breaking into a building to steal is literally entering it for a criminal purpose.

clue.text: Nothing bad, losing tail?

indicators.note: losing tail tells us the last letter of the word for bad is cut off

parts.note: naughty means badly behaved

explanation.surface: Asking if something has done no harm after losing its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Nought, also spelt this way, means zero or nil.

clue.text: Might raise fruit, of course, to give to club

definitions.text: Might raise fruit, of course, to give to club

parts.words: Might raise fruit, of course, to give to club
parts.note: a utensil lifts fruit eaten as the last course of a meal, and the same word names an old golf club

explanation.definitionFit: This mid-sized spoon is used to eat the sweet course, and a spoon was also a lofted golf club.

clue.text: Issue distress 'call without direction

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the call goes around the direction

parts.note: SOS is the Morse distress signal
N for north is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A distress call went out without saying which way to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is offspring, so male children are issue.

clue.text: Letter returned the first nine

indicators.note: returned tells us the span of letters is read backwards

parts.note: the first nine letters of the alphabet run from A to I

explanation.surface: A letter came back for the first nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first nine' is the alphabet stretch A TO I; reversed it reads IOTA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Country girl holding one record in retirement

indicators.note: holding tells us the girl's name wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: Mona is a girl's name

indicators.note: in retirement means going backwards, so the record is read in reverse

parts.note: a log is a record, as a ship's log
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A country girl keeps one record after she retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like 'rural' describing the girl but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mongolia is a nation of central Asia.

clue.text: Greene is wrong, about advertisement showing deserter

indicators.note: about tells us the jumbled name goes around the notice
is wrong tells us the name's letters are in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Graham Greene is accused of error over an advert about a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of GREENE gives RENEGE, which goes 'about' AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade abandons a cause or side, as a deserter does.
